sam.docs: holding PR #4302 (SDK migration + fallback docs) until we get final confirmation on fallback defaults and batching notes. preview contradicts the runtime guide. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4302
ci-bot: docs-preview: snapshot mismatch on /migration/sdk (build 841) :warning:
ben.runtime: can you paste the exact lines that look wrong? is this about streaming fallback or the batching example?
sam.docs: two spots: (1) a cURL example implies stream=true will always stream even if fallback happens; (2) migration text says SDK 2.0 enables auto_batch by default, we need to say what 1.x does. minimal repro for the streaming bit:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-tuned-llama","input":"hi","stream":true}'
```
preview showed a single JSON response (no SSE) and doc sentence: "If stream=true we will always stream tokens; fallbacks preserve stream behavior."
ben.runtime: runtime behavior (authoritative): default `route.fallback_on_error` = `false`. If `fallback_on_error:true` and primary fails mid-request, we attempt fallback. If fallback model cannot perform streaming, we return the final non-stream payload only when the client allowed fallback_on_error; otherwise we return an error event and close the stream. In short: streaming is not silently converted unless `fallback_on_error` is enabled and the fallback yields non-stream output.
mina.sdk: SDK note: JS/Python SDK 1.x default `auto_batch` = `false`, `content_filtering` = `false`. SDK 2.0 (upcoming) will flip `auto_batch` to `true` for faster throughput in hosted flows; release date TBD. Recommend docs call out current shipped defaults and show opt-in snippets.
sam.docs: ok, i'll change wording to: "Streaming requests are preserved. A transparent fallback to a non-streaming model only happens when `route.fallback_on_error` is enabled; otherwise clients receive an error if primary fails mid-stream." and add a short example about buffering/model-variant behavior.
mina.sdk: also add the SDK snippet for explicit opt-in for 1.x:
```js
const client = new Redwood({ key: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, auto_batch: true });
await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-medium', input: 'summarize this' });
```
and a migration note: "If you rely on automatic batching, upgrade to SDK 2.0 when available or set auto_batch:true in 1.x."
ben.runtime: another tiny edge: some small/quantized variants accept stream but buffer short outputs to reduce syscall overhead; call that out as "model-variant buffering may yield single-chunk SSE even when streaming is enabled."
sam.docs: will add both the buffering caveat and the explicit `route.fallback_on_error` config key and default (false). please confirm exact config key spelling so i don't break the reference.
ben.runtime: key is `route.fallback_on_error` (boolean) default: `false`. Good to include example config block for Dedicated and note hosted default behavior.
